messages:
Natalie M: Heads-up — product plans to push opal-18b to EU-edge next Tue. Early perf looks good but token/sec is higher than anticipated; want a quick capacity + egress sanity check before we lock the rollout window.
Samir K: quick first-pass estimate below, will refine with p99 numbers. main ask: how many GPUs and network headroom for steady vs peak.
Eli R: remind us of the perf baseline we should use (p95 vs p99, batch sizes, quant)?
Natalie M: benching on A100-80 int4. p95 ~8000 t/s, p99 ~6500 t/s per replica under our batching stack. use p99 for safety.
Samir K: rough calc (product expects 10k active sessions initially):
```
assumptions:
  sessions = 10_000
  avg req rate per session = 0.05 req/s
  avg response tokens = 400 tokens
tokens/s = sessions * req_rate * avg_tokens = 10_000 * 0.05 * 400 = 200_000 t/s
using p99 per-GPU = 6_500 t/s -> baseline GPUs = ceil(200_000 / 6_500) ~ 31 GPUs
apply operational multipliers: peak factor 3x -> 93 GPUs, regional headroom 20% -> ~112 GPUs
GPU-hours/day = 112 * 24 = 2_688 GPUh/day
GPU-hours/month ~ 80_640 GPUh
cost estimate (reserved @ $3.20/GPUh) ~ $258k/mo; spot avg @ $1.20 ~ $97k/mo
```
Anya S: re: network egress — we need to be careful, opal tends to expand tokens (structured outputs + subword expansion). let's do a clean token->bandwidth calc.
Frank W: quick bandwidth calc below — use avg token byte size 3.5 (UTF-8 + punctuation).
```
200_000 tokens/s * 3.5 bytes/token = 700_000 bytes/s ~= 0.7 MB/s -> 5.6 Mbps? wait unit check...
700_000 bytes/s * 8 = 5_600_000 bits/s = 5.6 Mbps (this seems low — re-check units)
Hold on: 200k tokens/s * 3.5 bytes = 700k bytes/s -> that's 0.7 MB/s -> *8 = 5.6 Mb/s per second. That is 5.6 Megabits/s.
But if responses are 1.4x input tokens on average, outbound tokens = 280k t/s -> 280k * 3.5 = 980kB/s -> ~7.84 Mb/s
Even at 1M t/s we'd hit ~28 Mb/s. Numbers are small per second but amplifications and TLS overhead + many replicas -> plan per-AZ egress headroom.
```
Anya S: I think the earlier mental calc that gave 64 Gbps mixed units. Frank's numbers are right for raw token bytes but we must add TLS, HTTP overhead, and S3 fetches for certain prompts. Also internal east-west for KV cache misses will add traffic. Multiply by ~2.5 to be safe.
Samir K: ok let's fold that in: 7.84 Mb/s * 2.5 ~ 19.6 Mb/s for outbound from a full cluster. That's still low vs our per-AZ bandwidth caps (we have 1-10 Gbps instances). main risk is sustained bursts and cross-AZ traffic.
Eli R: what about prefix cache hit rate? If cache hit is 60%, token generation drops a lot. We should run with conservative 40% cache hit for launch planning.
Samir K: recalculating with 40% cache hit:
```
effective tokens/s = 200k * (1 - 0.4) = 120k t/s
baseline GPUs = ceil(120_000 / 6_500) ~ 19 GPUs
peak 3x -> 57, +20% headroom -> ~69 GPUs -> GPUh/day = 1_656 -> monthly ~49_680 GPUh
```
Natalie M: good — that delta matters a lot for cost and capacity. Product will commit to a prompt-engineering pass to push cache hit >=50% before GA.
Frank W: next infra actions: 1) schedule a 2-hour soak test in eu-west with 60k sustained t/s and 180k peak; 2) validate KV cache hit ratios and origin egress patterns; 3) pre-warm autoscaler with a soft target of 70 GPUs so we don't cold-start.
Anya S: I'll open a runbook ticket and add network QoS rules for inference nodes. ops-bot: create ticket for soak test and autoscaler pre-warm?
ops-bot: Ticket created: INFRA-3347 — "opal-18b EU-edge prelaunch soak & autoscaler prewarm". Link: https://org.atlassian.example/browse/INFRA-3347
Samir K: owners: Anya (network/runbook), Eli (bench verification + cache metrics), Frank (soak orchestration), Natalie (PM/product coord). Can we have final trimmed numbers by EOD Fri?
Natalie M: yes, product will deliver optimized prompt set and realistic session model by Thu EOD. Aim to finalize GPUs & cost estimate by Fri.
Eli R: I'll push a staged perf run today using prod-like traffic generator and post results to this thread.
Frank W: also recommend a small canary for first 24h in one AZ limited to 10% traffic so we can validate tail latencies and eviction behavior.
Samir K: noted. I'll update capacity docs and send a short note to sales about preliminary cost implications.
Natalie M: thanks all — let's keep updates short in this thread. If anything blocks, ping @anja on-call. :thumbsup:
